did_you_know.text: The exact meaning of the name “El Shaddai” is uncertain. It is often translated as “God Almighty,” but its linguistic origin is debated.
“Abram” is commonly understood as “exalted father,” while “Abraham” is explained here as “father of a multitude.” This is a biblical wordplay connected to Abraham’s calling.
Circumcision was also practiced by other peoples in the ancient Near East, but here it receives a special meaning: a bodily sign of the covenant between God and Abraham’s family.
The word “sign” refers to something that recalls an identity or commitment. In this chapter, the sign is not an external object but part of a person’s body.
The phrase “be cut off from his people” is related to the biblical term karet. Its exact meaning varies by context and can describe exclusion from the community or a very severe punishment.
“Sarai” and “Sarah” are closely related forms of a name associated with a princess or noblewoman. The name change fits the promise that her role will extend beyond one family to many peoples.
Abraham’s laughter is connected with Isaac’s future name, which is related to “laughter.” The name preserves his parents’ reaction of surprise and joy.
Later in Genesis, twelve princes descended from Ishmael are listed. This fulfills in subsequent chapters the promise of twelve leaders among his descendants.
The phrase “on that very day” emphasizes immediate and exact action, without delay. Abraham does not merely hear the command; he acts on it that same day.
